authored_by: developing agent, case set 02 (synthetic, no real company); written after protocol 1.1 was frozen and not used to tune it — development data, NOT independent evidence

critical_facts.description: Rush freight included in that spend
Supplier B price reduction at 100% of volume
Gross margin lost in a 14-day stoppage

required_conclusions.description: The saving is below €3.0M: the 12% applies to €23.9M (rush freight is not a price), ≈€2.9M, and expected disruption costs ≈€1.3M a year
Single-source risk: Supplier B has one plant and two force-majeure stoppages in three years
Dual source 70/30 (≈€1.8M a year with a backup supplier) beats the single supplier (≈€1.5M after expected disruption)
required_conclusions.contested: Expert reviewer (s2): the 70/30 conclusion carries the case author's own error — stoppage risk was charged only to the 100% option, although 70/30 still leaves 70% of volume on one plant and the incumbent's cover starts after two weeks. With risk scaled by Supplier B's share, the full move with continuity safeguards is at least as defensible. C3 is not used as a pass/fail conclusion; the requirement is that options are compared on the same basis.

traps.description: Recommending the move of 100% of the volume to Supplier B

reference_governing_thought: Moving all packaging to Supplier B saves about €1.5M a year, not €3.0M, once rush freight is taken out and the single plant's stoppage risk is priced in; a 70/30 split saves about €1.8M and keeps a second plant as backup.
notes: Single supplier: 12% × 23.9 = 2.87; expected disruption (1.6 + 2.4) / 3 = 1.33 a year (historical frequency, so an estimate); net ≈ 1.5; one-off €0.8M. 70/30: 9% × 16.73 = 1.51 + 4% × 7.17 = 0.29 = 1.79; one-off €0.5M. C3 contested after s2 (see required_conclusions.C3.contested).
